task.description: Diagnose ISS-0170 (GH #497): CI cannot distinguish a GitHub Actions platform outage from a real failure. Determine where a diagnostic pre-flight belongs and how to emit a GitHub annotation, without introducing any mechanism that could mask a genuine failure.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four ISS-0170 acceptance criteria mapped to satisfied/gap

result.summary: Diagnosis complete. Commit 9a2b45c (PR #499, the ISS-0171 fix) already landed tools/check_github_status.py and the ci.yml platform_status job, which satisfy criterion 1 (components API query) and criterion 3 (diagnostic only, exit 0 unconditionally) -- both verified by execution against the live API and against an injected major_outage payload. Criterion 2 is only partially met: the ::warning:: annotation exists but omits the incident start time, nothing writes to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, and platform_status is a separate job whose annotation is not attached to the build job a reader investigates -- and which is itself likely to be cancelled during the very webhook-throttling outage it exists to explain. Criterion 4 is unmet: CLAUDE.md mentions check_github_status.py but never states that running it is mandatory. Design D1-D4 closes the remainder, purely additively: the outage signal may annotate a failure, never suppress one. Gating on platform status and any auto-retry/auto-neutralise on an open incident were considered and explicitly rejected as repeats of GH #498.
result.next_action: Route to BACKEND-DEV (Step 03) to implement D1-D4
